observations: Photo 0: A black game console held in a hand, side profile view showing a disc slot, eject button, and a rectangular warning/info label on the underside edge.
Photo 0: Console top surface is split between a matte textured panel and a glossy panel, consistent with the original Xbox One design.
Photo 1: Same console from a front-top angle with a black wireless controller resting on top of it.
Photo 1: Controller shows standard Xbox button layout (ABXY, two thumbsticks, d-pad, Xbox guide button).
No power adaptor/power brick is visible in either photo.
No game discs or game cases are visible in either photo.
No photo shows the console powered on or any screen output.

identity.kind: Xbox One console with one wireless controller

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a console matching the original Xbox One body shape; photo 1 shows one matching wireless controller.
No game discs, cases, or on-screen library are shown in either photo.
No photo of the power adaptor itself, and no photo/clip shows the console attempting to power on, so the nature/severity of the fault cannot be judged beyond the seller's own admission.

risks.risk: Console may not power on at all due to the admitted adaptor issue, or the issue could be in the console's internal power supply rather than just the brick.
risks.proof: A video clip of the console being plugged in and powering up to the home screen, or a clear photo of the adaptor plus a continuity/power test.

risks.risk: No games are visible despite being listed as included; discs could be scratched, missing, or not match the claim.
risks.proof: A photo of the 6 game discs/cases laid out, including FC visible by title.
risks.if_unproven: priced as console and controller only, with no games included

risks.risk: Controller functionality (sync, battery compartment, stick drift) cannot be assessed from a static photo.
risks.proof: A short clip showing the controller syncing and being used to navigate the dashboard.
risks.if_unproven: priced as controller of unknown working condition

risks.risk: Disc drive condition and internal hardware (HDD health, overheating/fan noise) cannot be seen.
risks.proof: A video of a disc being inserted and the drive reading/loading a game.
risks.if_unproven: priced as drive/internal condition unknown, worst case treated as faulty

risks.risk: Storage capacity (500GB/1TB) affects value but is not shown.
risks.proof: A photo of the rear/bottom label showing storage specs, or the console settings screen.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common capacity assumption

proof_requests: Video of the console being powered on with the current adaptor, showing whether it boots to the dashboard.
Clear photo of the power adaptor/brick itself.
Photo of all 6 game discs/cases laid out together.
Clip of the controller syncing and functioning in-game or on the dashboard.
Photo of the rear label or settings screen showing storage capacity and serial.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as an Xbox One console with one controller, but the seller's own admission of an adaptor issue combined with no proof of power-on, no visible games, and no adaptor photo means it must be priced at worst case as a non-working unit with accessories unconfirmed.
